question: On games that were already played and stored, do the two promotion-leaf terms and the anchor-attack penalty actually occur on the played path, so that the source-level finding has a reachability statement rather than only a type statement?
no_new_search: The scan replays stored move lists only. No search, no game generation, no fitness evaluation.

design.deduplicate: a game is identified by (seed, depth, game_index, tuple(moves)) so the served-blind-reasons files, which replay the same games with extra termination metadata, are not counted twice
design.replay_precondition: each stored move list is applied with apply_action on a reconstructed start position; the replayed terminal status and winner must equal the stored ones, else the game is recorded as a problem and excluded from the counts
design.position_scan: the start position and every position after each stored move
design.promotion_leaf: for every unpromoted piece whose base type has a positive promotion gain, record whether square_index is in the evaluator zone (live branch, bonus weight*unit), and otherwise whether the intended half-bonus condition would hold if Square targets were compared as indices (dead branch)
design.anchor_term: record whether anchor_square(owner) lies in the opponent pseudo-attack map (the -weight*10 penalty)
design.weights: EvaluationConfig defaults as used by the stored games: promotion_potential_weight=3, anchor_escape_weight=5, hand_weight as recorded in each file's design

endpoint_written_before_the_run.decision: leaf_terms_occur_on_stored_game_paths if at least one position exercises the live in-zone branch and at least one exercises the dead half-bonus condition, else leaf_terms_are_absent_on_stored_game_paths; in both cases report counts and the number of distinct games and rulesets involved
counts_to_report: games scanned, games passing the replay precondition, problems
promotable-piece observations, of which in-zone (live) and half-bonus-intent (dead) and neither
distinct games and seeds with at least one live in-zone observation, with at least one dead-branch observation, and with at least one anchor trigger
endpoint_written_before_the_run.what_this_cannot_establish: not utility, not outcome effect, not search-behaviour effect, not a strength claim; a term that never fires on these paths may still fire elsewhere and a term that fires need not change any chosen action
